reason: Redeploy steps for the suaranetijen staging host were repeated by hand across sessions (drain Horizon, compose up --no-deps, migrate, nginx reload, public 200 checks). Consolidating into one project skill so the order and the nginx-IP gotcha are not rediscovered.

Post-deploy page served stale SSR-less shell from page cache (x-page-cache: HIT) after SSR container recreate; the redeploy skill had no cache-flush step. Added flush step and markup-level verification.
Agent held a staging deploy until the Wikidata enrich batch finished because recreating the app container would kill it. Make that gate an explicit first step.

Worker hosts have different compose paths per user (not a single shared /home/dev path). The redeploy in this episode resolved each worker's directory via the compose label and then drained and recreated it, which worked on all three hosts. The skill only said "same on worker hosts", which does not give the path or the order.

After pulling a new :latest, compose reported the SSR container as Running without recreating it, and the deploy went on to a healthy check. The skill's up -d step does not warn that a Running line can hide an old image.

A redeploy produced a Dead app container, a 502 for about 10 minutes, and unstarted scheduler/ssr containers. The skill had no recovery path for a Dead container and no check that all services came back up.

Session deployed PHP 8.5.12 to main + 3 workers. User overrode the one-host-at-a-time order to parallel ("paralel. ini kritikal"); the skill had no rule for that, so the agent had to improvise. Parallel is allowed on explicit request but per-host gates stay.

Worker w3's compose pinned `azmifauzan/suaranetijen:flare-fix-2d054d5`, which was not in the registry. Pull failed, the pipe to tail masked the failure, and the worker came back on the previous PHP 8.5.10 image. Caught only because the agent ran php -v afterwards.

Runtime security patch (PHP 8.5.10 -> 8.5.12 for CVE-2026-109618/109619): the only reliable proof of the fix was `php -v` inside each container, and that is what caught the stale w3 worker. The skill checked public status but never the runtime version. Renumbered the following step to avoid duplicate numbers.

The skill was triggered only by "redeploy"; a CVE-driven runtime patch to staging and workers is the same procedure but the user words it as a security patch, so the skill would not be recalled for it.

Step 13 compared a container's image ID with RepoDigests[0] (manifest digest), two different identifiers, so the check reports a mismatch on every correct deploy and invites needless force-recreates. This episode's worker2/3 check printed IMAGE_MATCH=NO while the digests agreed; the operator had to fall back to RepoDigests by hand.

The push was from a dirty tree with an uncommitted Welcome.vue change. Building from the working copy would have shipped unreviewed edits, so the agent built from `git archive HEAD`. The skill never says to do this, so a future deploy can silently ship WIP.
Folded into staging-operations; detailed runbook carried in references/redeploy-runbook.md.
